text:
Last night's Integration Debt Night at Kestrelmoor's Flatiron office pulled about 60 people, and the room stayed sharp the whole way through.

Two ideas stuck with me.

Priya Raman-Holt (VP Platform, Tallowbrook) runs 140 partner integrations with a team of three engineers. How? "We stopped building connectors one by one and started publishing a spec. Partners build to it now."

Marcus Feldane (founder, Quillary) argued that agent pilots fail at the integration seam, not at the model. His team's rule: wire up data access before choosing a model.

Then came the show of hands. About 40 of the 60 people said an agent pilot at their company had stalled on getting data access. Not model quality. Access.

The best part was the disagreement. Priya thinks partners should own their connectors. Marcus thinks the platform has to own them, or quality drifts. Neither budged, and I'm still turning it over.

My takeaway for anyone selling or buying AI right now: the unglamorous plumbing decides whether the pilot ships. If your agent story doesn't start with data access, it's probably starting in the wrong place.

Thanks to the Kestrelmoor team for hosting.

Who owns the connector in your world, the platform or the partner?
